post.text:
I sell cement at the market here in Abeokuta. A customer came to pay for 150 bags of cement, collected receipt and disappeared for over 4 months.

Yesterday, he came back with trucks to carry the cement. He said he had been seriously sick since the day after he made payment,
post.author_description: Legal Practitioner⚖️/ Influencer/Stories/Politics/ Relationship/ Advocate for fairness & due process/ Liverpool fan. YNWA❤️

botInput.comments:
**@enyola** (@enyola)  
If the price of cement had gone down, will she give him extra bags of cement to balance the difference?  
Likes: 2097 | Reposts: 27 | Replies: 55

**@jerrymejh** (@jerrymejh)  
The delay works in your favor. 4 months is unreasonable. You should argue that the customer's failure to collect the cement within a reasonable time breached his side of the agreement, exposing her to storage costs and market risk she never agreed to carry.  
Likes: 956 | Reposts: 24 | Replies: 113

**@AJLordship** (@AJLordship)  
Supply that man his cement to the last bag. Prices had gone up since he made his payment - Agreed. You collected his money & have been trading with the money. His money you have been training with has earned you both profit and interest. You'll do yourself a favour by supplying the man his cement before he goes legal.  
Likes: 567 | Reposts: 17 | Replies: 37

**@ade_bronco** (@ade_bronco)  
A bargain is a bargain. The only thing you can legitimately charge him for is storage space. His cement staying in your shop took up space you could have used to store new purchases.  
Likes: 411 | Reposts: 4 | Replies: 19

**@HerRoyalDupcy** (@HerRoyalDupcy)  
If he paid in full and collected receipt, honestly the cement belongs to him already. Unless there was an agreement that payment expires after some time, asking him to add money may not really stand legally.  
Likes: 93 | Reposts: 0 | Replies: 0

**@temmyt007_** (@temmyt007_)  
Simple! Charge him for demurrage (cost of storage) per bag per day. ₦50 per bag per day should be fair. 4months is about 120 days. Total storage cost should be about ₦900,000 for the 150 bags over 4 months. Ask him to clear the bill so that you can release his goods.  
Likes: 51 | Reposts: 5 | Replies: 19

**@Aularmy** (@Aularmy)  
Oga, once payment don complete and receipt don enter hand, that cement don become him own legally. Price increase painful, but you can’t suddenly change deal after 4 months because market change. If receipt no get collection deadline, the man actually get strong case. Next time, put expiry date for collection on every receipt. Na that one go save you from future wahala.  
Likes: 49 | Reposts: 0 | Replies: 0

**@VikyInsights** (@VikyInsights)  
Supply him his cement purchased... Or you will do jail😂😂😂  
Likes: 39 | Reposts: 0 | Replies: 4

**@DrModibbo1** (@DrModibbo1)  
Give him the cement at the price he bought and charge him for storage for 4 months to recover your balance.  
Likes: 34 | Reposts: 0 | Replies: 0

**@ala_nso** (@ala_nso)  
You’re charging him for the wrong thing 😂! You have sold your market and receipt issued so businesses has been concluded, but however he didn’t pay you for keeping the goods in your warehouse, so you can charge him extra for storing his goods in your warehouse, charge him as logistics companies does, but again you’re a fool for treating a customer who bought so much cement from you like that?  
Likes: 32 | Reposts: 0 | Replies: 5
